hard.q: Correct the mistake: If I had a headache, I will take a pill.
a: If I have a headache, I will take a pill.

hard.q: Correct the mistake: If you leave milk in the sun, it goes sour.
a: If you leave milk in the sun, it will go sour.

hard.q: Change to the third conditional: If I win the lottery, I will travel the world.
a: If I had won the lottery, I would have travelled the world.

hard.q: Make the result negative: If he eats too much, he will feel sick.
a: If he eats too much, he will not feel sick.

hard.q: Change to the third conditional: If he forgets his keys, he will stay outside.
a: If he had forgotten his keys, he would have stayed outside.

hard.q: Make the result negative: If you eat healthy food, you will stay fit.
a: If you eat healthy food, you will not stay fit.

hard.q: Correct the mistake: If I will go to the bazaar, I will buy some apricots.
a: If I go to the bazaar, I will buy some apricots.

hard.q: Correct the mistake: If the students did their homework, the teacher will be happy.
a: If the students do their homework, the teacher will be happy.

hard.q: Change to the zero conditional: If he asks me, I will help him.
a: If he asks me, I help him.

hard.q: Make the result negative: If you mix red and blue, you will get purple.
a: If you mix red and blue, you will not get purple.

hard.q: Change to the zero conditional: If you ask nicely, she will help you.
a: If you ask nicely, she helps you.

hard.q: Make a question about the result: If you eat healthy food, you will stay fit.
a: Will you stay fit if you eat healthy food?

hard.q: Rewrite starting with the result: If you add sugar, the tea will taste sweeter.
a: The tea will taste sweeter if you add sugar.

hard.q: Correct the mistake: If you will ask nicely, she will help you.
a: If you ask nicely, she will help you.
